comment:
Both times I’ve visited this park I have absolutely eaten shit with in the first 15 mins. Which is weird but not totally off brand. 
Trail is dry during the summer and nice for the area. Paid parking required
Great hike!!! Watch for poison ivy, but views were great and trail was well maintained:)
Great hike! Approx half wooded half in a more meadowy area
Great trail with semi groomed paths. Great river and scenic views. Mix of open field, forest, and river portions.
Beautiful trails - some sections easy and some more technical
55 pounds and a wife for the first time JAX carried his weight pack so his training has now started as well.
Great little RUCK with 55 pounds, maybe 53. Two dogs and an actual endangered species joined me as well… A wife. It was nice to have her along. For the ride.

Trail was quite wet but I was able to keep my barefoot shoes dry even through the muddy sections. The right hand loop was quite soft and I was disgusted to see multiple tissue paper in different parts of this beautiful trail. I did pick them up on the way back with a couple of sticks but it's really gross to see how much garbage is continuing to be accidentally dropped or blatantly left behind has been steadily increasing since more ethnic communities find this trail. I can't help but think there is a correlation. Aside from that this was a, nice solid hike and absolutely loving this 40 pound weight vest that my wife purchased. I took that and my backpack over top, carrying close to 55 pounds total. Felt great in barefoot shoes and it was nice to be sore from carrying the weight this morning and then get right back out there and do it again. Start building a little bit of muscle while I'm hiking is the best possible scenario. I hope to wear this thing every time going no matter what the distance until my trip in May and then carry it on when I get back. Maybe I should carry it the entirety of 2026.

A few spots washed out and muddy 
But otherwise a great trail with nice views along the river. Great hike
Beauty adventure with my boy. Loved my Pine needle tea.
Still pretty muddy in spots. Other than that, well maintained
Parts of trails are closed but not clearly marked
First time doing the big loop in a while. Felt good to get back out there. Once I get a couple of injuries to heal up a bit I'd love to get back out there with my weighted backpack.
Great trail. Went during the muddy spring months. Some parts do tend to flood when during/after a high rainfall or snow melt.
Beautiful winter hike. We were in snow shoes but good boots would work well too ❄️
Snow-packed trails; icers and poles were helpful
Paid parking off Gideon
Beautiful trail but definitely needs to be better marked
A little muddy unless it’s been dry out

The trail is well maintained and pretty open. Not too many areas of roots/rocks/treacherous walking. River is beautiful, it’s been a dry summer so the trail is dry and dusty in some areas. Good change of scenery, from open field/space to forest, to pine forest. Lovely spot!
Amazing provincial park just outside London and this trail was amazing hike some hilly spots and great views
Incredible day for Komoka Provincial
It is Monday. I leave 3 AM Wednesday morning for my trip. Eight days off gray backpack. Bring on La Cloche  silhouette trail

Another excellent training session for this before we head off grid for 90+ kilometres in Killarney.  First session with our real gear and real packs and the dogs were loaded with food not just weight this time. Nice that we've been training with heavy weight because my pack felt light with real gear instead of weight room plates. Excellent training session today as long as my feet hold up without blisters this will have definitely been my best training session yet for the upcoming trip
Lots of rolling hills on soft path in the shade
Great day for another 9km push through the park.  North loop is open again and the bridge looks great!
It was great, don’t get lost on other trails keep an eye on your maps
Nice hike with variable terrain. Lots of shaded portions throughout

Parking seems confusing,  using the QR code?  Great conditions today.  Not busy , especially when starting next to the river and doing the full outer loop.  They had the full loop to the right of the parking blocked off when I started at noon ?
Great warm-up with my two dogs as the first time we've hit the trail since we have confirmed our September trip to La Cloche Silhouette Trail in Killarney.
What a great RUCK. 45 pounds in my backpack and both dogs had a good bit in their saddlebags.
Great ruck
Gorgeous Trail and perfect time to get out early and beat the heat with my two animals.
Lots of ticks, so make sure you check yourself and your furry friends.
Komoka Provincial Park is the perfect place to start your long hike experiance , good for kids, dogs, anyone really. Great photos and wide variety of Native species to photograph and draw!!
Nice trail many variations to go. Dogs loved it

Super pretty. Lots of variety and change with meadows, woods, river. Mostly dry and well maintained, quite muddy in a couple of areas. Trails marked in a very confusing way — we ended up off the trail entirely a couple times. Love a loop- and there are a few. So you can do the whole thing or shorten it up if you need to. A couple of great little picnic beach spots. Definitely moderate climbs in some areas — otherwise an easy walk. Missing star was due to the poorly marked trails.
Well maintained, pretty views, and lots of bridges!
Nice trail
Very popular  trail but well maintained and beautiful nonetheless! No bugs on a cooler day towards the end of May.
One of the best hike. Weather was perfect cool and sunny especially around the woods.

Easy trail, a couple of decent hills. Well marked and traveled. Most of it was shaded but started off in open fields under direct sun. Liked the boardwalks, don't find those in a lot of parks. Poison ivy along in the field areas and along the sides of the trail.
Segment along the water was nice, bound to see a deer! Parking is $6.50 for 2 hours, and you can make your way through the trail in under that time without rushing. Could be a great trail run too.
30lb ruck, first time at this location...loved it...good elevation change...great workout
Great trails!  Love it :)

Some light interval jogging or in the first day without the weighted backpack but also the first time I’ve done the whole path in a while. Made it here at 6 AM for sunrise and then driving home at 7:21. Fantastic way to start the day.

Excellent jaunt with my three dogs, sorry two dogs and my wife. =D 

Nice to squeeze in a good adventure before heading to work today
Lovely Easter weekend hike!
Epic ruck with 65 lbs with my out of town cousin Lauren who made this an absolute treat by fitting it in on a Friday morning.
Pleasantly surprised! Beautiful hike.  Blue trail very muddy but the rest was ok.
Great job with my two dogs carrying their saddle bags with weight on myself with a weighted backpack and shorts no shirt in -8°C weather. Gorgeous evening and the body loved it.

Respect to my friend Greg coming out for a nice long and heavy ruck today in treacherous frigid conditions. Treacherous conditions with the rocks and the frozen ground and the light snow had each of us falling multiple times. 6 total I think. Only drew blood once . He took a weighted backpack for the first time & mine was 93 lbs -holy cow. I did give Greg the two 10 pound dumbbells about 75% of the way along so that would’ve dropped my weight to 73 pounds for the last 3 km. Didn’t realize how much until we got back and weighed myself on the scale. Most weight I’ve ever done and longest ruck yet. 

Welcome back anytime Greg. LFG. 

Personal best for weight and personal best for length of HEAVY RUCK￼.
Home track great for running.
Great RUCK with my son Robert and another four guys carrying 58 pounds to 90 pounds on a rotating basis, trading dumbbells of 10/20 back and forth.
Absolutely beautiful trail, will do again! Hiking boots are highly recommended, it gets muddy to some places. The map was useful.
First time to this trail.. nice to have a little challenge with a few inclines
Very nice trail, done it twice now. It is well kept
Beautiful woods, well marked trails, lots of trail route options
Watch your step at komoka. Lots of hidden roots. Komoka always delivers.....sprained ankles lol
Nice early morning wruck with a 35 pound backpack and a couple of dogs.
The parking method is tedious, especially if you don't have a parks account. Parking lot almost full, but trails not crowded. Some nice views of river and fall foliage. Some hills.
Favourite trail this time of year!
Great spot just outside London. A few small hills but really great!
Amazing trail for practice if you want to go for bigger ones.
Trail close by and convenient.
Beautiful, scenic trail ~ met and walked with some friendly locals along the way :)
Perfect day for a hike. Great conditions.
Can’t use the washrooms they are so smelly

Lovely woods hike, mostly shaded, a few choice spots to see the river. Well maintained, assorted bird calls and wildflowers along the way. A little buggy, but it’s their house; we’re just visiting! Muddy in places and it can be visually monotonous, hence the four stars.

Clean trail, well marked. Bathrooms and garbage available at parking area. The trail is well traveled but much of the time you're alone without anyone in view. Lots of dogs but all were  leashed and passing was respectful.
Amazing trails, a little muddy on the right side of the main fork. Not too busy on a civic holiday. Paid parking
Trail was great lots of nice shade walking path in spots could use work.
Great spot.
It’s going to take a second visit to cover all the trails. We did the south perimeter. The North side would have added another hour.
Only a few muddy patches on the first loop,otherwise good hike as always!

The littlest bit muddy in some spots with recent rain, but overall great conditions and so many options for different length loops.  Some elevation changes and one decent set of stairs but nothing strenuous.  
Lots of well organized parking and washrooms available at entrance.
FANTASTIC TRAIL. Views 100. Terrain 100. Vibes 100.
Tough one after doing a  10.77 km right before in barefoot shoes.
nice cool trail, I would consider it moderate quite a bit of up and down. it is well kept, lots of trees.

The trail is great with lots of inclines and interesting terrain. there were two parts however that we had to turn around. one section was so muddy and doing down a hill there was literally no way through so we had to turn around. there is another section of the trail that was really over grown and not well maintained. you can see in the photo I posted, where we turned around. for this reason it only gets 4 stars from me. overall the trail was fantastic though and I will be back.
nice transitions between environments. Short and long loop together will take about 2hrs.
Beautiful and easy trail, lots of options for longer or shorter hikes
peaceful!
Beautiful and easy trail, it great condition
Trail in great condition, well groomed and well marked. Went early morning, no bugs.

Absolutely awesome Trail as always and even though this is the most water I have ever seen directly on the trail it was beautiful. Gave my barefoot shoes a nice test by dipping them in the river to see how they stood up. Top marks

Nice little early morning jaunt with the boys through the woods in my barefoot shoes. Had some bigger boys with us today so the time wasn’t where it’s at when I’m on my own but it was a good route and pace to get the heart rate up on a hot Sunday morning.
The trails are decent, and one hill was complete mud which resulted in backtracking. Not worth paying $6.50 to park.
Beautiful day for a hike

Mild mannered little hike around a pretty good spot on the river. Some elevated areas to check on your fitness. some very moist areas where, if one might have brought a mud phobic dog, said dog would have the potential to miscalculate a jump and send both of you careening down trail.  Thankfully there are some river bank accessible points to wash off- that is IF you were the one to bring that type of dog. 
Animals: two male cardinals, lots of chickadees, a squirrel, and one human male.

Some muddy areas which is expected this time of year. Not well marked in some spots but all trails always make it easy to stay on which trail colour you pick. Beautiful spots along the river and so many beautiful trees in bloom
There is no other attractions in this park other than hiking trails and the river.
Amazing walk in the rain. Made me want to do more hikes in the rain.

• trail is pretty muddy at some points but not to difficult to navigate around. 
•a few frog, snakes, snails, and pretty flowers 
• some pretty inclined areas that are not to hard to get up but are quite the workout!
Dry & since it’s a Monday there are not a lot of people.
Friday’s storm downed a few trees and created a few swamps that made parts of the trail impassible. Overall good though!
Muddy
Trail was good - not much mud at all!

I've enjoyed this trail several times. each time a different season of the year. it was six degrees today and there was a small amount of mud on the Blue trail. no garbage and  quiet! trail took me 2 hours
Little muddy but a great place for a hike
Mix of hard-pack snow/ice and mud - spikes are recommended as the slopes are slippery.
Snow is a bit packed down creating slippery spots, was very glad to have my spikes on. There were a few muddy spots, nothing terrible. An absolutely gorgeous trail.
Lots of people, lovely river views,  muddy at times, lots of fun!
several wet muddy stretches on the eastern (Oxford) loop, otherwise excellent conditions
Muddy in a few places but overall not bad. I wore my trekking shoes & didn’t have any deep puddles
Still a little muddy in sections. Boots are highly recommended!
So gorgeous today! Lots of people and dogs. Trails were nice and packed down.

Beautiful trail with the fresh snow, easy to moderate for this area if you go right first, if you go left mostly downhill paths..   There is one section by the river that was unclear the safety to pass due to river Creek.. So we backtracked and went around. 

Better signage for the offshoot trails might be helpful. But it's otherwise well marked

Winter hiking on this trail was amazing. If you take the time to look around you and notice the wildlife, amazing. Serene  surroundings. Pet owners on this trail extremely courteous with some of the most well behaved dogs. Moderately challenging hills and slopes can be slippery with snow at times. Definitely will return
Dress for the wintery conditions and good winter boots to enjoy the trail. Some spots were a bit wet/icy and snow covered.  Take your time to enjoy this hike.
Packed snow made hills a bit slippy - spikes will be helpful
Bit slippery in spots, probably should have put my spikes on my shoes. But an absolutely beautiful hike anyways.
Little snowy but well maintained trail with a few people and plenty of parking space
The blue trail was a lot muddier than the white trail
Best trail around us considering the proximity to our house. First time back here since training for our backpacking trip back in September.
A very beautiful hike, I came across a garden snake and deer. Very picturesque and stunning views of the river. The colours of the trees were changing so it was a gorgeous golden yellow scenery.
Well marked and well maintained. No mud. Lots of loops to the trail that you can shorten and length trail length. Really nice trail
Moderate trail with many high vistas of the Thames river. Lots of options for routes and length. Paid parking through Ontario Parks web site was a bit of a pain
Fantastic day for a hike!
Trail conditions are excellent  - dewy in places, but no mud.

Another great training run for the big one at the end of the month. 50 pound backpack and two dogs. Perfect water bottle to practice for the big back country trip. Would love to bring the nine-month-old puppy at the end of the month but she proved again today why she is a liability. She’s great for a little help On the hills but the puppy in her make sure a liability too many times. To help on the hills does not cancel out the delays. She stays home at the end of the month.
Parking fees applied - thru QR code - a bit fiddly to register.
Great hike. Some parts of the actual trail did not match the published trail. For that reason  I gave 4 instead of 5 stars.
Can be a bit muddy
Great trail-easy to moderate! Bring bug spray and watch out for poison ivy!

The entire Komoka White Trail Loop has an impressive amount of biodiversity in one hike. Beautiful fields excessively populated with Monarchs, giant old oak trees, and wild walnuts.

The east end of the loop is pretty hilly, with unexpectedly jagged terrain & hills. The west loop is flat, easy to walk through, but QUITE SUNNY!! Bring a hat & water!   Also $6.50 for parking.

Overall great trail. Love this one :)

For the most part, excellent trail conditions with occasional muddy patches. Some of the boardwalks, bridges and stairs require maintenance. Blaze markers are clear and sufficiently frequent to aid navigation.
Full of nature
Beautiful trail. Well marked and pat down. A few trails have been closed off for trail regeneration but otherwise beautiful.
Trails were nice and clear! No mud to be found!

Variety of things to see. Lota of open spaces, forest and follow part of a river.
Great park would definitely come back
Pay parking. Either get a Ontario Parking Pass or spend 20 mins on phone at trail for one. Ugh! $6.50 for 2 hours. Otherwise trail was nice. Lots of shade and some sun
Some steep hills. Lots of wildlife and great views:
Roots

Great trail along the river! Some side trails closed and if you do the big loop it has parts in an open field with grass. If you stay on the small loop most of it is in the trees though. Larger hills on the big loop too. Has a few nice spots further in that go right along the river and our dog was able to go in.
Almost ideal trail conditions — a few small muddy patches on the White trail near the old Oxford parking lot. LPS training ongoing today but no impact for day hikers.
Lots of mud!

Part of the trail is fully washed out, and the water is fast flowing nearby. Keep dogs at arms reach when by the river. 

Other than that, wonderful, as per usual!
Parking meter broken so you have to pay online. $5.25 for 2 hours.
Great walk in the woods and along the river. Recommend walking poles and/or icers as some sections slippery
Muddy!
little muddy this time of year but otherwise lovely hike
Muddy, some wooden bridges. Amazing exercise and views.
Was terrific!
Great trail, clear and wide
A great trail with all kinds of different types of sights beautiful views of the river goes up-and-down on the back part of the loop quite busy
Some part were closed for regeneration. Other marked areas were overgrown from lack of use. Otherwise a good trail.
Beautiful trail, well maintained and saw lots of turkeys and a deer!
Pretty good hike, hills weren't too bad and there was a lot of wildlife.
Most of the trail is shaded. Some areas with tall grass and the path is narrow so check for ticks after!

Only did the first loop, but it was awesome! It switched from white trail marks to blue after going up the stairs. Super well maintained, and has a bit of everything: hills  boardwalks, views, access to the river. Would highly recommend sunscreen, and bug spray if you're super sensitive to bug bites
Hike was ok, should be rated easy. Missed the last 7km as I didn’t realize we had to leave the park - map kept telling me to go onto private property that was fenced in. Nice walk in the woods.
Beautiful park...lots of rolling hills and the river has lots of little hidden nooks.
Beautiful.
great trail. great day.
quiet not good for bikes
A pretty trail. Not very difficult. Reasonably well maintained. Quite busy. saw cute baby raccoons.

Very beautiful trail, open field areas, a running river, and covered forests
Note: don’t do on scorching day

Northern part of the trail and along the river was great! Busy, but to be expected with one of the first nice weather days. Tried to do the full 17km but the south end was pretty narrow for me and Walter (Great Dane) and had to cross a busy road so we headed back instead.

I've always loved Kamoka. The trail isn't that busy, has decent elevation change, and nice bridges and walkways mixed in. 
*Note: provincial park pay trail. It's just under $6 for 2 hours in the park and increases from there.*

stay right at beginning of trail from parking lot for the most scenic part of the trail which follows along part of the Thames River.  if you do not want to continue to complete the entire loop back to the parking lot I suggest you follow the same path back. .  the second half of the loop has many hills, valleys and not as scenic
Trail was a little wet, lots of rain last night. Overall in great condition!

Trail is great for a day trip. There are a few more trails to explore in the park as well. It was mostly flat with just a few inclines and declines. The park does require you to pay for parking per hour though.
Beautiful trail! Icy in spots, but worth it to check out!
often busy, but enjoyable. can get muddy or slushy depending on time of year.
Good trail
Muddy today but still awesome!
Pretty muddy some spots overall great trail and well kept.
Quite muddy but good workout
Nice trail, pretty good signage. Enjoyed it, I'll be back
It was great! Stay on the white path, it goes right along the river, it’s beautiful!
Great trail
great trail.
Great trail though not well marked. Variety of elevation

Good trail, challenging and lots to see. Very busy today. Park Ranger was on site to give tickets to those who didn't pay, or who took too long. She said she handed out 27 tickets today. This is a pay to Park trail.
Good exercise, not particularly scenic, $5.25 for 2h parking
Good trail. Hot and humid today. Cut hike shorter than hoped
The north west loop is well maintained and has a lot of side trails. Had to walk on the highway to get to the the southern loop and it was not really worth the hike.
Very hot, bring a hat! And bug spray! But was very beautiful and long
An absolutely fantastic loop, especially for photographers! One side takes you along the Thames River and the other brings you through a meadow. Absolutely great for bird watchers!
muddy in a few spots but overall what I expect for this spot
Great trail with many different route options. Lots of different wildlife. Elevation change is fairly challenging compared to many other trails in the area.
good
Beautiful!
well maintained trails, well-marked, but we only noticed a trail map at the entrance.
nice but very hot out in the open stretches on the way back.
Amazing!

Ok trail. Best part was near the tree covered river side. Lots of flowering trees on orange and blue trails meadow side. Smells amazing and can hear bees buzzing away happily. Lots of variety in the left loop. Bathroom at parking lot. Parking: near bathrooms there is a machine where you enter your license plate number and is on a one hour, 4 hour, day pass style. We did 4 hours for $7.50. I think it was $14 for the day and $5 for an hour. Can use credit card. Trail to the right was not as good as the larger loop to the left but still was ok and challenging... very steep hill included.
great weather and great hike. Trail very quiet and peaceful in a Thursday evening. Loop North of parking lot not recommended for younger kids/toddlers, very steep.
not a bad trail. a little more difficult then expected but well worth it.
Perfect conditions today
Slippery in rain today, watch the wood parts
Really well maintained, liked that the bathrooms were open, will love to go back
Not the best for biking, but not bad. Some muddy and steep areas. Pretty good overall.
Lots of open areas exposed to the sun but could stay on trails near the water for more shade. And be prepared for ticks, they're here!
Very beautiful .
Nice trail! There are multiple steep climbs at some points so be prepared. Didn't get to see much wild life, unfortunately. Very busy, so might want to keep your mask handy when passing people.
I enjoyed every bit of the walk and the scenery. Muddy in some places which was absolutely OK. Recommend it!
Not too muddy! Perfect day!
Really nice variety of views
Very nice
Beautiful afternoon for a hike at Komoka Provincial Park.
A great trail to explore in the winter. Even saw a bald eagle
Nice mix of hills and flats   Not icy today but cleats nice
Perfect with spikes!
Icy, muddy
icy in spots.  would be good to have spikes on your footwear
Was really good! Quite icy is some spots! Recommend bring skates or a third leg.
Some places where icy & others were muddy
Great conditions! Mild winter day.
Gorgeous early winter hike.
5 trees down on path after wind storm but non issue
Watch for horse manure.  It is paid parking $5-$6 credit card pay too
Very good trail condition. There are a few hills. But overall very easy. Pay for parking or you will get a ticket.
Bit muddy
great hike even in the rain. few deer and 100's of robins
Some very steep areas that are not easy for all
Beautiful trails. Gorgeous fall colours. Easy hike, you can choose which trails you take to customize your length of walk.
Did hiking yesterday. Beautiful fall colours , not busy, easy level,normally it takes me 2.5 hours. Yes you have to pay entrance fee.

some trails are not marked properly
some very dangerous trails near cliffs beware of bringing younger children on this trail
Gorgeous! Headed left from the parking lot this time and it was full of beautiful surprises and a variety of terrain.
Clearly marked. Great fall views and lookout points. Not a super busy trail on a friday evening. Have to pay for parking but fairly reasonable for the care of the trail.
Beautiful!
Perfect today
Have to pay to park. 5 stars otherwise
Great trail.. I would say moderate and not “easy” in a few spots.
Slippery this morning
Beauty hike! Never ceases to amaze me. Get some beautiful views from some of the higher up spots.
Great hike! Must pay to park (someone was giving out fines for cars without tickets). Also the parking is like 2km before where the directions takes you.
Beautiful hike, not too muddy even though it just rained
Awesome trail. Paid parking. Flat ground with roots. Mostly shaded.
Usually this app has the trails marked really good. This time not so much
Trail is great.  Beautiful and interesting. Maps are nonexistent.  Even this AllTrails map is not accurate. Main entrance trail not shown.  Can get very confusing.

My mom and I have been in plenty of hikes, but this is the first logged hike of ours in All-Trails. This was such a beautiful trail. Beautiful water views and a bunch of moths and butterflies out to play. The hills were a challenge but they got us slightly ready for our Sleeping Giant hike next week!

Really nice location outside London. There’s a fee to park to start but a big lot. The first half is really nice with decent size paths through the woods. The second half is mostly through long grass fields. It’s really pretty but there are signs warning of ticks. Would probabaly just go back through woods next time.
Well maintained! I didn’t know parking wasn’t free until I got there but otherwise nice place! Lots of great views :)
Fantastic trail.

CoVid update - Park is open. Washrooms were open with hand sanitizer inside the washroom. Park entry was free. Parking lot on Gideon had a LOT of cars and we ran into quite a few people (on a Wednesday daytime) but were mostly able to pass with reasonable spacing.

Started the hike around 5pm today April 1st. Was a beautiful day for hiking.  Wore shorts and a tshirt and brought a hoodie. Amazing scenery with very few people. Maybe 5 people  in two separate groups. Walked 8 plus miles in roughly 2.5 hours. Multiple stops throughout. Gorgeous sunset.
Beautiful hike! Lots of bridged and runs along the river! Second half is a bit less desirable but still a nice walk. A bit muddy had to pay $5 to park
Take the outer loop, some great surprises along the way.  It gets moderate due to tight path.
Great trail. Parking lot is now located closer to woodhull. Parking machine accepts coins only. Would hike again!!

Parked on Oxford Street W. just east of Woodhull Road and walked the short distance back to the old entrance to Komoka Park. Parking is free on the road but not at the main parking lot off of Gideon Drive. Walked the white and blue trails.
great trail just outside of the city. There are multiple trails for different skill levels, I brought my dog along and he loved it. I reccomend this trail!
One half was great. Niece fell into a washed out section on the other half. Would describe this trail as moderate. Lots of steep sections.
Definitely some upkeep needed, especially for the price of parking.
Outer loop of Komoka Park. White and Blue trails combined for an 8.5km loop from the NEW parking area on Gideon. Used for testing out gear setups; should take about 1 1/2 hrs to complete.
